title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the opening page of a self-contained treatment of the Cartier operation. All rings are F_p-algebras. The aim is to compute the de Rham cohomology of an A-algebra B that admits a p-basis, as the first step toward the Cartier isomorphism H^*_DR(B/A) ≅ Ω^*_{B^{(p)}/A}.

(a) Let B be an A-algebra and set Λ = A[B^p] ⊂ B. For b in B we have d(b^p) = p b^{p-1} db = 0, and da = 0 for a in A. So the differentials of B/A and of B/Λ coincide: Ω^1_{B/A} ≅ Ω^1_{B/Λ}, hence Ω^*_{B/A} ≅ Ω^*_{B/Λ} as differential graded algebras. The de Rham differential is Λ-linear, so H^*_DR(B/A) ≅ H^*_DR(B/Λ) as Λ-algebras (a fortiori as A-algebras).

(b) Suppose there is a one-element p-basis x, with a = x^p in Λ. Then B ≅ Λ[X]/(X^p − a).
- Ω^0 is Λ-free with basis 1, x, …, x^{p-1}.
- Ω^1 is Λ-free with basis dx, x dx, …, x^{p-1} dx.
- Since d(x^k) = k x^{k-1} dx with k invertible for 1 ≤ k ≤ p−1, the forms dx, …, x^{p-2} dx are exact, and the cycles in degree 0 are exactly Λ.
- Hence H^0 = Λ·1 and H^1 = Λ·[x^{p-1} dx], both free of rank 1.

(c) For a general p-basis (x_i)_{i∈I}:
- Ω^1_{B/A} is free on the dx_i.
- B ≅ ⊗_Λ B_i with B_i = Λ[x_i] ≅ Λ[X_i]/(X_i^p − a_i), so Ω^*_{B/A} ≅ ⊗_{i∈I,Λ} Ω^*_{B_i/Λ} as differential graded Λ-algebras.
- The Künneth formula then gives H^*_DR(B/A) ≅ ⊗_I H^*_DR(B_i/Λ).
- Consequently H^* is the exterior algebra over Λ on the classes [x_i^{p-1} dx_i].

The next page defines the inverse Cartier map ψ: Ω^*_{B/A} → Z^*, with ψ(x) = x^p and ψ(dx) = x^{p-1} dx. After base change by Frobenius it gives φ: Ω^*_{B̃/Ã} → H^*_DR(B/A). This page's computation is what shows φ is an isomorphism in the p-basis case.
errors: Minor: in (a) the isomorphism H^*_DR(B/A) ≅ H^*_DR(B/Λ) is stated 'comme A-algèbres'. It actually holds as Λ-algebras, which is what is used in (b)–(c).

Gap (easily filled): Künneth over Λ requires flatness or splitting. This holds because each Ω^*_{B_i/Λ} is a complex of free Λ-modules whose cycles, boundaries and cohomology are free direct summands. The infinite tensor product over I is understood as a filtered colimit of finite ones; this is not stated but is harmless.
The decomposition B ≅ ⊗_Λ B_i is used implicitly. It is the definition of p-basis (the monomials x^α with 0 ≤ α_i < p form a Λ-basis) and is not proved here.

ideas.what: Differentials of B/A equal differentials of B over A[B^p]
ideas.where_published: Katz, 'Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem' (Publ. IHES 39, 1970), §7

ideas.what: De Rham cohomology of Λ[X]/(X^p − a): basis 1 and [x^{p-1} dx]
ideas.modern_name: local computation for the Cartier isomorphism

ideas.what: Künneth reduction for an algebra with a p-basis, so that H^*_DR is the exterior algebra on [x_i^{p-1} dx_i]
ideas.modern_name: Cartier isomorphism in the p-basis case

deep.surprise_reason: This is a textbook-standard proof of the Cartier isomorphism for algebras with a p-basis, essentially identical to Katz 1970 §7. It is correct and complete as a sketch, but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line a): 'Soit B/A, dans, posons' is probably 'Soit B/A, et posons' (or 'on pose'); the reading of the abbreviation is uncertain.

In the basis of Ω^0_{B/Λ}, the image shows an overwritten or crossed entry near x^{p-2}, x^{p-1}. In the Ω^1 line, a stray crossed-out 'x^{p-1}dx' fragment appears; the final intended lists are 1, …, x^{p-1} and dx, …, x^{p-1}dx.
Line b): 'formée d'[-un-] élément x' – the word after 'd'' is crossed or overwritten. The meaning is 'formée d'un seul élément x'.
